claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers under sustained loading is governed by the degree of short-range order within the layers.
Enhanced short-range order increases local lattice distortion at FCC/BCC multilayer interfaces.
The lattice distortion produced by enhanced short-range order raises the barrier for dislocation nucleation at multilayer interfaces.
Elevated dislocation-nucleation barriers produce more gradual and homogeneous plastic flow.
Lower short-range order reduces interfacial lattice distortion and dislocation-nucleation barriers.
Reduced dislocation-nucleation barriers promote abrupt, localized dislocation activity and strain bursts during sustained loading.
As-deposited CoCrFeMnNi-based FCC/BCC HEA multilayers possess inherent short-range order and lattice distortion.
Controlled annealing can create a higher-SRO state relative to the as-deposited multilayer.
Annealing can enhance short-range order without disrupting the nanoscale multilayer architecture or changing other relevant microstructural features.
The degree of short-range order modulates deformation resistance within dislocation slip systems.
Short-range order controls cooperative interactions between dislocations.
Annealed high-SRO multilayers will exhibit smoother creep curves, more gradual deformation, and lower strain-rate variability than the as-deposited baseline.
High-SRO multilayers will show a delayed onset of significant dislocation nucleation at FCC/BCC interfaces.
As-deposited lower-SRO multilayers will exhibit more abrupt dislocation bursts and localized plastic deformation.
The short-range-order state will correlate with the spatiotemporal evolution of interfacial dislocation density.
Stress and temperature materially influence HEA creep behavior through atomic mobility, diffusion, and activation of deformation carriers.
